title: Meeting Dizzy and sending him in as his substitute
summary: Chick Webb rejects Dizzy, Bauza recalls meeting Gillespie at the Savoy and has him sub for three days.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Dizzy in the meantime, after me, he sees Chick Webb.

Yeah, to get in -- how can I get a break? How can I get a break? But Chick didn't like Dizzy. Chick said, no, I don't like that for my band. I don't want anybody (inaudible) couldn't do nothing, Chick's band.
: When did you meet Dizzy Gillespie?

Oh, well, I met Dizzy in 1935, '34, '35. He was working with Teddy Hill at the Savoy, and I felt like this. This is (inaudible), this is the evolution of the music. But those guys used to, you know, they used to talk bad about him. They didn't like (inaudible) this guy, he's crazy, plays some crazy stuff.
And I said, no, this guy don't play no crazy. This
guy, he's got something in there the people ain't caught up with yet. The musicians got to get down, and the guy's a hell of a musician.

So I said to him, Dizzy, the only thing I can do to help you to prove yourself, I will do something, and let's see if it works. I went there to substitute a man (inaudible), and I worked three days, and then I end up getting the job. Now, I'm going to simulate that I'm sick, and I send you to work in my place.

He say, hard book. You got to play first in everything. Nobody else play first in there. You've got to play first. You've got to play the show, you've got to (inaudible) the show and then play it fast, and you've got a few little solos, because (inaudible) used to play some beautiful solos, and I played more like in the style of Doc Cheetam, you know, (inaudible), you know, nice and all that.

So see what you do. Don't go overboard. So I sent Dizzy in there. Three days later I came back to work. Cab come and say, hey, how you feeling? Back to work? I say, yeah, I'm feeling better now. I was feeling bad in the stomach, maybe something I ate -- you know, lies. I went and had my ball.

So he said, you know, that guy you sent ain't bad. I say, the guy's terrific. That's a hell (inaudible). I said, I want you -- want to hear that from you. That guy is something else. You haven't heard anything yet.
